svg.title: boxscore puzzle
svg.desc:
The mark: a boxscore with one cell deduced.
It has to survive 16px, and that decides everything about it. A favicon is read at a size where individual strokes disappear into texture, so the only things that carry are the ground colour, the silhouette, and one high contrast element. Three columns by three rows is the most grid a 16px tile holds before it blurs into a solid block.
The colours are the product's, not a palette chosen here. #1f362e is the header ground from serve/ui/phone/tokens.css, the band across the top of every board, and white is the header ink. A mark in colours the interface does not use is a mark that belongs to nothing.
The bright cell is the whole idea and there is exactly one. The product is deduction: a grid of numbers where you work out the one you do not have. Two bright cells would read as a pattern; one reads as the answer. It is bottom right because a boxscore's totals are, so the silhouette says "a table that adds up" rather than "a window".
No digits. At 16px a numeral is three grey pixels, and a mark that needs to be read is a mark that fails at the size it is actually used.
AT 16px THE DEDUCED CELL MERGES, and that was seen and priced rather than missed. Rendered at 16, 32, 48, 64, 128 and 180 and looked at on both a light and a dark ground: from 32px up the bright cell separates cleanly and the mark reads as a boxscore with one answer in it. At 16px it reads as a grid, which is still the product and still distinguishable from a ball or a diamond, but the idea that makes it this product is gone. Accepted because a modern tab is 32px on any hidpi display and 16px is the icon in a bookmark list. If the 16px case ever matters more, the fix is fewer and bigger cells, not a brighter one: the contrast is already maximal.
Written in desc rather than an XML comment on purpose: the first version put this in a comment, every dash pair inside it made the file invalid XML, and the browser served a parse error page that the rasteriser then turned into a 98 byte icon. The numbers said it was written. Only the picture said it was an error page.
